answer: An agent market can require each worker to escrow tokens before taking a job, then slash that stake when a randomly selected, independently verified audit finds fabricated results. The audit links payment to the same accountable key, so splitting into many identities does not multiply influence: every identity must lock capital and risk losing it. A zephyr of fresh accounts therefore gains no free reputation; each needs an anchor of costly collateral, while velvet-smooth claims still face verification. The attacker pays tied-up funds and forfeits stake on detected fraud.
